The thirty-credit program will prepare students for meaningful careers in the burgeoning fields of UX/UI.

Students emerge from this program as versatile professionals capable of addressing complex design challenges.

Armed with the knowledge of both UX and UI, graduates become adept at designing solutions that merge aesthetics, functionality, and human-centered values.
The program is unique in its emphasis on the ethical implications of research and design processes and products.

UX courses guide students in creating designs that prioritize inclusivity, social justice, sustainability, and user well-being.

In an ever-evolving technological landscape, the Master of Arts in UX/UI Design equips students to stand at the forefront of innovation, transcending traditional boundaries between the two fields.

To the best of my knowledge there are four other higher ed institutions in RI that offer World Language Education programs: Salve Regina, Rhode Island College, Providence College and Roger Williams University.
None of these programs is new: such programs have been in place for at least 10 years.
In all those cases, the original World Language programs were part of the Secondary Education programs, just one of the multiple tracks that students could take.
Two of those institutions have already taken steps to adapt to the new RIDE certification reality.
Recently, in both Salve Regina and RIC the World Language Program has become independent.
According to the information listed on their websites, the World Language Education program is still a track of the Secondary Education Program in the cases of both Providence College (<https://academics.providence.edu/secondary-education/>) and Roger Williams University (<https://www.rwu.edu/undergraduate/academics/programs/secondary-education>).

The new URI World Language Education program will fill a void that currently exists in the world language teacher preparation programs by focusing on providing more comprehensive preparation to our candidates so they can be effective teachers at the elementary and secondary levels, and it will allow us to continue being the leader in preparing future world language educators in the state of RI.

The RIDE certification requirements for World Language teachers are:4 ● Bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution ● Completion of an approved program or Credential Review Consortium Institution (CRCI) credential review plan for the preparation of All Grades World Language Teachers in a specific language ● Completion of a minimum of 12 weeks of student teaching in this area and a minimum of 60 hours field experience prior to student teaching ● Demonstration of meeting the pedagogical competencies of the Rhode Island Professional Teaching Standards (RIPTS) ● Demonstration of meeting the content competencies as prescribed by the American Council for the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) Other requirements: ● Meet all Rhode Island pedagogy and subject matter testing requirements for this certificate area 4 See: <https://www.ride.ri.gov/Portals/0/Uploads/Documents/Teachers-and-Administrators-Excellent-Educators/Educator-Certification/Cert-Requirements/tbd_AG-World%20Languages-Req.pdf?ver=2015-01-22-123036-823>.
